findings.note: TestResultSchemaVersionDistinct's second half is vacuous, and its comment claims otherwise. The comment (manifest_test.go:109-111) says "Validation must read ResultSchemaVersion, not the manifest's own SchemaVersion. The two are equal today, so only a result carrying ResultSchemaVersion proves which constant the check uses." But SchemaVersion = 1 and ResultSchemaVersion = 1 (manifest.go:23 and :27), so a result whose SchemaVersion field is 1 is literally indistinguishable under the two constants: the accepting half passes identically whether validateResult compares against ResultSchemaVersion or SchemaVersion. The test cannot detect the drift it was written to pin, and it reads as if it can. Pinning it would need a compile-time assertion that the constants may diverge, or a build-tag fixture where they do.

findings.note: The write_results helper in the new shell test takes two parameters that no call site ever passes. ONLY (argument 3, consumed as the `only` shard filter in the embedded node script) and SKIP_CROSS (argument 4) are both defaulted to empty, and all four invocations in the file pass exactly two arguments, so the partial-results and no-cross-shard branches of the helper are never executed. That is untested code inside the test harness itself: if either branch is wrong, nothing notices, and a future reviewer will reasonably assume they work. Either drop them or add the negative case they were clearly written for (a plan with one shard result missing already has coverage in the Go tests, but not end to end).

evidence.note: every call site passes only repo and plan

findings.note: The Go-floor scan's try/catch comment is wrong about what it guards. `fs.readFileSync(file, "utf8")` does not throw on binary content — it decodes lossily, substituting U+FFFD — so the catch never fires for the "binary" case the comment names; it only fires for a genuinely unreadable path, such as a tracked file deleted from the worktree. The practical consequence is that every tracked binary is regex-scanned, and any byte sequence decoding to `Go 1.NN+` inside one would fail the manifest gate with the message "<binary file> advertises Go 1.NN+ but go.mod requires 1.26" — a claim about prose, pointed at a file that has none. The repo has no such binary today, so this is latent rather than live. A cheap fix is to read as a Buffer and skip anything containing a NUL byte.

evidence.note: catch comment claims binary files are skipped
readFileSync with utf8 encoding does not throw on binary input

findings.note: The rubric blocks on the diff introducing unsafe execution such as eval, and the new shell test does contain the token. It is a deliberately assembled fixture, not executed code: `printf 'value := %s(untrusted)\n' eval > "$repo/src/staged.txt"` writes the string into a throwaway git repo under mktemp so the deterministic lint has something to fire on, and the file's own comment says the pattern is assembled so this file does not carry it literally. Nothing is evaluated; the fixture repo is removed by the EXIT trap.
